lines.en: Pandemonium--and yet a dumb show. Terror and frenzy had stolen everyone's hearing. They surged toward the exit, intent only on escaping the hall, but somehow avoided jamming the doorway and spilled out onto the wooden street.

lines.jp:
と、幸運はそこまで、板敷きの通りに出た途端、下級水夫の一人が雨に濡れた木板に足滑らせて転倒───そこへ、ザウエルの広間より抜け出してきた大海蛇が迫る。
　魁偉な頭をのたくらせ、全身を大きく波うたせ、空気を嗅ぎ回るような挙動は芋虫や子蛇がやるなら可愛げも見えたかも知れないが、五米級の長物がやると凄まじく不気味な迫力が宿る。
lines.en:
Their good fortune ended there. The instant they reached the plank road, one young sailor slipped on the rain-slick wood and fell. The great sea serpent slithered from the hall of Zauer and bore down on him. 
It waved its grotesque head, its whole body rippling broadly as if sniffing the air. A caterpillar or tiny snake might have looked almost charming doing the same, but from a five-meter monster, the motion carried an appalling, sinister force.

lines.jp:
ただ迫り来る異形の迫力に転倒したまま竦んでいた少年水夫へ、巨体を利して雪崩かかって囓りついた、わけではなかった。
　彼の前で鎌首をもたげ、どこかご機嫌を窺うようにそろそろと下ろして吻の先を触れさせただけ、鼻先を押しつけただけ、と見えたのに。
lines.en:
It did not use its massive body to crash down on the terrified boy and bite him. 
Instead it raised its head before him and slowly lowered it, almost as if testing his mood. It appeared merely to touch him with the tip of its snout, pressing its nose lightly against him.

lines.jp:
瞬間。下級水夫は海老ぞりに、背骨が折れるのではと言う恐ろしい勢いと角度で。指先まで逆に反り反っているのに、悲鳴の一つもない、のは、口を限界まで開けて硬直しているからだった。
　び、びんっ、と短く詰まった痙攣で、どんと倒れて動かなくなった。
lines.en:
In that instant, the young sailor arched backward with such terrifying force that it seemed his spine might snap. Even his fingertips bent back, yet he uttered no scream, for his mouth was locked open to its limit. 
After two short, taut convulsions, he collapsed with a thud and lay still.

lines.jp: 下級水夫が顔面を打ちつけた鈍い衝撃音で、音が戻ってくる。
lines.en: The dull impact of the young sailor's face striking the ground brought sound back to everyone.

lines.jp: 「なんだ!?　ありゃあ、電気喰らった時みてえな……野郎っ！　ありゃあ電気鰻かっ!?」
lines.en: What was that!? It looked like he'd been shocked... Damn thing! Is that some kind of electric eel!?

lines.jp: 「こいつはまさか、ロックフォールの言ってた……？」
lines.en: Could this be what Rockfall was talking about...?

lines.jp: 巨大な海蛇は、倒れ伏した下級水夫の前で鎌首をもたげると、ああ見よやその異様な頭、逆三角形の頭部は、いかなる奇怪な筋肉と靱帯を骨格構造を有しているのか、鋭角の円錐状に収縮したのだ。
lines.en: The giant sea serpent raised its head over the fallen sailor. And what an unnatural head it was: through some bizarre arrangement of muscles, ligaments, and bone, the inverted triangle contracted into a narrow cone.

lines.jp: 騎乗槍の切っ先の鋭さと、ゴム質の弾力を兼ね備えた頭の先で、撃ち斃した下級水夫の体表を嗅ぎ回り、彼が身に着けた水兵服に暫時戸惑っていた様子であったが、すぐさま嗅ぎ分ける魔性の感覚、半ズボンの裾から細く尖らせた口吻の先を潜りこませて、小さな尻のあわいへと押し進めていく───
lines.en: Its rubbery yet lance-sharp snout probed at the fallen sailor. It hesitated briefly over his uniform, then, guided by some uncanny sense, began seeking a way beneath his clothing--

lines.jp:
「だめえええっ、誰かぁ……！　誰かぁ！
　誰でもいいよ、あの子を助けて、
　優しくって、仲間想いの良い子なんだ」
lines.en:
No! Somebody...! Somebody! 
Anyone, please, save him! 
He's a kind boy who always looks out for his friends!

lines.jp:
「この前みんなが食中毒で死にかけた時も、
　あの子はみんなの汚れ物の世話、
　全部してくれた───」
lines.en:
When everyone nearly died of food poisoning the other day, 
he was the one who cleaned everything up for us! 
He did it all--

lines.jp:
「食べられちゃうよう、
　なんだかすっごい卑猥なやり方で、
　あの子が食べられちゃうようっ」
lines.en:
It's going to eat him! 
In some horrible, obscene way, 
it's going to eat him!

lines.jp: 大切な仲間の危機に何も出来ない非力に歯噛みしおろおろ救いを求める下級水夫の手を、優しく取って、力強く頷いた頤がある。端正な手であったし、繊細な線の横顔だった。大海蛇を指差して、語り出すは。
lines.en: One sailor wrung his hands in helpless anguish and begged for someone to save their precious comrade. A graceful hand gently took his, and a delicate profile nodded with confidence. Pointing at the sea serpent, she began to explain.

lines.jp: 「あれは円口類、それも始原の一種でしょうね。あの類の生き物は、獲物の皮膚を擂り鉢状の歯で食い破り、あるいは体腔から頭部を侵入させて」
lines.en: That is a jawless fish, probably a primordial variety. Creatures of that kind use their rasp-like teeth to break through a victim's skin, or else enter the body through an existing opening--

lines.jp: いつの間にか、そう、いつの間にか、なのだ、この娘の登場というのは。いる時には、気がつくとそこにいる。この時も、黒髪のしなやかな姿が、逃げ出しかねて留まる一行の中にいつの間にか入り交じってあり、
lines.en: Somehow, without anyone noticing--that was always how this girl appeared. Whenever she was present, people simply looked up and discovered her there. Now, too, her lithe, black-haired figure had silently mingled with the crew members who could neither flee nor stay.

lines.jp: 「つまりは口とか肛門とか性器とか。体の穴から何らかの消化酵素でもって、体内の肉や内臓を溶解させて啜り取る───後に残るのは、骨と皮ばかり」
lines.en: In other words, through a natural opening. They use some kind of digestive enzyme to dissolve the flesh and organs from within and consume them. All that remains afterward is skin and bone.

lines.jp: 「ああ、つまりは。この島に残っていた、奇妙なくらいに綺麗に骨だけ残った死骸達、あれらは恐らくあの生き物に捕食されたのね」
lines.en: Ah, so the strangely clean skeletons left around the island were probably the remains of creatures it consumed.

lines.jp: 「ってことはあの子、お尻から、中味、全部吸い取られて───ぅ、うぷっ！」
lines.en: Then it's going to get inside him and dissolve everything--urk!

lines.jp: 「うぶ、うえええええええ！」
lines.en: Ugh--bleeegh!

lines.jp:
密航者の大海蛇の生態を語る口ぶりは、乾いて散文的な言葉で構成されていたけれど、この場合誇張がないのはかえって空恐ろしい。
　伝えられた事実の無慈悲で容赦なく、また直接にその情景を目の当たりにしつつあるだけに水夫君達のおぞましさいかばかりなものか、堪えきれず吐き戻す者まで出たのも無理はあるまい。
lines.en:
The stowaway described the sea serpent's biology in dry, prosaic terms. In this case, the lack of exaggeration only made her account more horrifying. 
The facts were merciless, and the sailors were watching the scene unfold before their eyes. Their revulsion was understandable; some could bear no more and vomited.

lines.jp: 「……長々とようもまあ、有り難いご講釈、有り難すぎて涙が出るぜ、おう、お前なんでいる」
lines.en: ...Well, thank you for that long and very helpful lecture. So helpful it brings tears to my eyes. And why the hell are you here?

lines.jp: 「それに、ようもウチの水夫に上等な口叩いてくれたの、このメス餓鬼がぁ！」
lines.en: More importantly, how dare you say all that to one of our sailors, you little brat!

lines.jp: 「あれ？　私の言った事、どこかに間違いがあったとか……？」
lines.en: Huh? Was something I said incorrect...?

lines.jp: 博物学の考査ならば問題なく点をもらえただろうが、憂えるべきはそこではない。それとも単純に積極的な被虐嗜好者という度し難い人種で、故意にやっている事を隠しているだけなのか、懸念に瞼に映した翳りは青磁を思わせて薄蒼く、すこぶる付きの美を宿したが、美しい娘を女衒に叩き売りにする事だって平気の平左でやってのけそうなのが信天翁号の船員であり、水夫長もこの時朔屋へ唇の端を吊り上げながら、
lines.en: She would surely have earned full marks on an examination in natural history, but that was not the concern. Or perhaps she was one of those incorrigible people with an enthusiastic taste for mistreatment and was only pretending not to provoke them deliberately. The anxious shadow in her pale, celadon-blue eyes gave her exceptional beauty. But the sailors of the Albatross were the sort who might sell a beautiful girl to a brothel keeper without batting an eye. The boatswain curled one corner of his mouth at Naomasa.

lines.jp:
「……おう、朔屋。良いこと思いついたぜ。
　このメス餓鬼をな、こうやって」
lines.en:
...Hey, Sakuya. I just had a good idea. 
We'll take this little brat and do this.

lines.jp: 言うやいなや、密航者の首根っ子と腰の革鞄をがっと掴み、軽々と、高々と頭上に持ち上げた水夫長の膂力、攻城弩の弦を引き絞る巻揚機の様に筋肉の束を浮き彫りにして、
lines.en: The moment he spoke, the boatswain seized the stowaway by the nape and by the leather bag at her waist. With astonishing ease, he hoisted her high over his head. Bundles of muscle rose across his body like the windlass drawing back the cord of a siege crossbow.

lines.jp:
「あ、痛い痛い痛い、
　首がお腹が締まって息が───
　なに？　私をなにする───あ───」
lines.en:
Ow, ow, ow! 
My neck, my stomach--I can't breathe--
What? What are you going to do with me--ah--

lines.jp: 水夫長にぶん投げられ、大海蛇に着弾する密航者。滑る肌の上で電撃の迸り、弾き飛ばされたものの、何故だか平気だった。むしろぴんぴんとしていた。派手な悲鳴で粘液まみれ、なにかしら卑猥な眺めだった。
lines.en: The boatswain hurled the stowaway into the great sea serpent. Electricity flashed across its slick skin and flung her away, but somehow she was unharmed--positively lively, in fact. She shrieked theatrically, covered in slime and presenting a vaguely indecent spectacle.

lines.jp: 「ぬるぬるっ、ぬるぅっ、あああ服が髪が体中が、粘液で、悪臭放つ粘液で、ぬっるぬっるぅ……」
lines.en: Slippery! So slippery! Ahhh, my clothes, my hair, my entire body--all covered in foul-smelling slime! I'm completely drenched in it...

lines.jp:
「……なんで生きとるんじゃあいつは。
　しかもあの海蛇、あれにゃ興味を示さんとくる。海蛇ですらあいつは好まんか」
lines.en:
...How in blazes is she still alive? 
And the sea serpent doesn't even care about her. Not even that thing finds her appetizing.

lines.jp:
「水夫長、水夫長、今の投擲で、
　敵は一瞬怯んだようでありますが、
　しかし敵は極めて損耗軽微、
　戦友をどうか助けて下さいでありますっ」
lines.en:
Boatswain, sir! Your projectile 
appears to have startled the enemy momentarily, 
but the enemy has sustained almost no damage! 
Please save our comrade, sir!

lines.jp: 密航者を投げつけられた衝撃で大海蛇は一度は下級水夫から身を引いたものの、黒髪の娘の方にはそれきり興味を失ったか、獲物と見なさず、中断された食事に戻ろうと、再び下級水夫へ這いずり寄っていた。
lines.en: The impact of the stowaway had made the great sea serpent pull away from the young sailor once. But it seemed to lose all interest in the black-haired girl, not even recognizing her as prey, and began crawling back toward the sailor to resume its interrupted meal.

lines.jp: 「つったってもおめえ、見ての通りのでかさに加え、電気まで撃ってきやがる」
lines.en: You say that, but look at its size--and the damned thing can throw electricity around too.

lines.jp: 「皮も分厚い上に、豪いぬるぬるしてるもんだから、こんなピストルじゃ弾も徹らない」
lines.en: Its hide is thick and incredibly slippery. Bullets from little pistols like ours won't penetrate it.

lines.jp: 「ああいうのに、どこまで保つかわからないけど。……やるしかないか……？」
lines.en: I don't know how long this will work against something like that... but do we have any choice?

lines.jp:
双子がなにか意を決しかけたところで、近くの廃屋からふらりと出てきた人影、着馴らして形の崩れた着物に袴の姿は、飄々とした気風さえ漂わせていたけれど。
　げふうと漏らしたおくびには品も慎みもあったものかで、おまけに熟柿を潰したようにぷんと臭った。したたかな酒を流しこんだ後に特有の。
lines.en:
Just as the twins appeared to reach a decision, a figure wandered out of a nearby abandoned house. His well-worn, shapeless kimono and hakama gave him an almost carefree air. 
Then he belched, without the slightest trace of manners or restraint, releasing the cloying smell of crushed overripe persimmons--the particular odor that followed a great deal of strong liquor.

lines.jp:
「騒がしいなあもう。
　てめえら、人が気持ちよう、
　酒喰らってりゃあ、ばたばたと」
lines.en:
You're all so damned loud. 
A man is in there enjoying 
a nice drink, and you go stampeding around...

lines.jp: 「あっ。近頃姿が見えず、酒もなくなっているかと思ったら、あんたかぁ！」
lines.en: Ah! So that's why no one's seen you lately and all the booze has been disappearing! It was you!

lines.jp:
大海蛇の恐怖とか下級水夫の悲劇とか、そういう深刻な事態へ、酔っぱらいが道端の雑草に小便をぶちまけるような、どうにも場にそぐわぬ詰問をここで浴びせる、朔屋も朔屋。
　それを無視して生欠伸で胸元をばりばり掻いていた智里だったが、皆がなにやらあまりにも進退窮まった感に包まれている、睨み据えている奴がいる、と大海蛇の方へ振り向いて、びくりと肩を震わせた。
　さしもの智里でさえも───
　　　　　　　　　　　　と思いきや。
lines.en:
Faced with the terror of the sea serpent and a young sailor's tragedy, Naomasa chose that moment to interrogate him, as wildly out of place as a drunk relieving himself on roadside weeds. 
Tomosato ignored him, yawned, and scratched noisily at his chest. Then he noticed everyone looked utterly trapped, staring at something. He turned toward the serpent and jerked his shoulders in shock. 
Even Tomosato, of all people--
                Or so they thought.

lines.jp:
「アあん、なんだぁあのコウガイビルのでっかいなぁ……っぶ、ぶひゃひゃひゃひゃひゃ、
　あっはっはっは。おい見ろあの頭」
lines.en:
What the hell is that, some giant hammerhead worm...? B-bwahahahaha! 
Ahahahaha! Hey, look at its head!

lines.jp: また皆に振り向くなり、しゃがみこんで片膝ばんばん叩きながら、指さして大哄笑の、指さされるまでもないし、そもそも笑えるような段でもない、のに殺し屋の笑いは遠慮がなさ過ぎた。
lines.en: He turned back to the others, crouched down, slapped one knee, pointed, and roared with laughter. No one needed him to point it out, and the situation was not remotely amusing, but the killer's laughter knew no restraint.

lines.jp:
「へのこだへのこ、ちんぽこだ、魔羅だ。
　あっはっはっはっは、
　なにこの淫獣、腹いてぇ」
lines.en:
It's a prick! A great big prick! 
Ahahahahahaha! 
What is this filthy beast? My stomach hurts!

lines.jp: 殺し屋の笑声は爽快とか痛快とかそういうものではなく、破壊的ですらあった。ただの馬鹿笑いだった。この男、場の空気をたたき壊す事に関しては、朔屋に並ぶものがある。
lines.en: The killer's laughter was neither refreshing nor exhilarating. It was positively destructive--nothing but idiotic cackling. When it came to demolishing the atmosphere of a scene, this man could rival Naomasa.

lines.jp:
「……あーあ。
　誰もが思ってたけど口には出してなかったこと、言っちゃったよあの人」
lines.en:
...Oh, great. 
He just said what everybody was thinking but had the sense not to say aloud.

lines.jp:
「馬鹿やめろおい、せっかく腹に入れた酒が、
　全部逆流するだろうがあっはっはっは」
lines.en:
Idiot, stop! All the booze I finally got into me 
is going to come right back up! Ahahahaha!

lines.jp: さらには、下級水夫をも辟易とさせる言動のみならずこの男、自身が物理的な破壊力まで縦横に駆使するので手に負えない、立ち上がったその時には、例によって例の如く、現れた時には居合わせた全員が様々な角度で無手である事を見ていたはずなのに、あの定寸を越えて長い刀をいつの間にか手にしていた。
lines.en: As if behavior obnoxious enough to appall even the ordinary sailors were not bad enough, the man could freely wield literal destructive power as well. When he stood, as always, everyone present could have sworn they had seen him empty-handed from every angle when he first appeared. Yet somehow, he now held that extraordinarily long sword.

lines.jp:
「……ンの野郎。
　たたっ斬っちゃる」
lines.en:
...You bastard. 
I'll cut you to pieces.

lines.jp:
眼差しを七分眼にすれば眸の蒼の揺らぎが凝縮されて、すぅ、と動き出せば燐光の軌跡さえ置き残す、智里は、大海蛇へと歩を進めている。
　居合わせた者全員の、意識の虚ろを衝いた動きの起こりで、あ、と気づいた時には、無造作としか言い様のない足取りで大海蛇の眼前に、その知覚でさえ、蒼い眼の男が動き出したと思った次の瞬間には目前にあったようにしか感じられなかったろう。
lines.en:
His eyes narrowed, condensing the wavering blue of his irises. When he glided into motion, even a trail of phosphorescence seemed to linger behind him. Tomosato advanced toward the great sea serpent. 
His first movement caught a hollow instant in the awareness of everyone present. By the time they noticed, he had already arrived before the beast with steps that could only be called casual. Even to its senses, it must have seemed that the blue-eyed man began to move and then, in the very next instant, stood directly before it.

lines.jp:
剣尖が描く円弧は大きく滑らかで、けれど誰にも智里がいかなる剣の入りで斬撃を放ったのか見えたものはおらず、見たのは智里が振り抜いた刀を脇に、自然にこちらへ戻ってくる姿と、大海蛇の頭部の根元辺りに深々と刻まれた斬撃の線ばかり。なにやら去勢されたかの。
　智里の剣は人間のみならず、劫初の恐怖を、その身に纏う電撃ごと斬り伏せる、ように見えて。
lines.en:
The arc drawn by his sword point was broad and fluid, yet no one saw how Tomosato initiated the stroke. They saw only his blade already swung through at his side as he naturally walked back toward them, and the deep line cut near the base of the serpent's head, as though the creature had been castrated. 
Tomosato's sword appeared capable of striking down not merely a human being, but a primordial terror and the electricity that clothed it as well.

lines.jp: 大海蛇に浮いた斬撃の線はあっさりと薄れて消えた。
lines.en: The cut across the great sea serpent simply faded and disappeared.

lines.jp:
「あ、あれ？
　今、斬れてたよね、間違いなく」
lines.en:
H-huh? 
He definitely cut it just now, didn't he?

lines.jp:
「おうとも。剣閃、しっかり抜けてたぜ、
　だが……」
lines.en:
He sure did. The stroke passed clean through. 
But...

lines.jp:
「───なにあの人。斬れ味よすぎて、斬れたのにまたくっついてるじゃない。
　凄すぎて逆に駄目の好例だ」
lines.en:
--What is with that man? His blade is so sharp the two sides joined back together after he cut it. 
A perfect example of being so good that it becomes useless.

lines.jp:
「だが、今のでちっとは怯んだようだ。
　───今だ、あの水夫、
　拾って逃げるぞ！」
lines.en:
Still, that seems to have stunned it a little. 
--Now! Grab that sailor 
and get out of here!

lines.jp:
たとえばそこが海の上ならば。あの道化た悪魔が真剣に造りだしたかのおン襤褸船信天翁号にあるならば。どのような死地を迎えようともせせら笑って切り抜けて、あるいはついにその褒められた物ではない人生の最期を迎えようとも、死神に唾吐きかけて、冥界の河の渡し賃さえ、酒に替えて海にぶちまけてくれと願う無頼の徒であっても。
　陸の上では本来の剛胆も半減すると見えて、逃げるわ逃げるわ、木造の通り、雨に濡れた板敷きに足を取られ、泡を食って這いずって、逃げる。海の無法者共と言うより、戦国の世の塗炭に苦しんだ百姓の逃散めく。
lines.en:
Had they been at sea--had they been aboard the battered Albatross, as though some clownish devil had built the wreck in deadly earnest--these ruffians would have laughed their way through any mortal peril. Even if their disreputable lives finally ended, they would have spat in Death's face and asked that the fare for crossing the river to the underworld be traded for liquor and poured into the sea.
 On land, however, their native courage seemed reduced by half. They ran and ran, losing their footing on the rain-wet planks, panicking, crawling, fleeing--less outlaws of the sea than peasants abandoning their villages amid the ruin of the warring states.

lines.jp:
背後に迫るは、信天翁号の船員達の誰も聴いた事がないような───いや、機関長は知っていたか、ともかくも造化の神のいかなる悪意か、この時代まで生き残っていた太古の捕食者。
　一行の前に姿を現した時は、まだ寝惚け眼だったと言わんばかりに速度を増して追随する、下級水夫の中に絶望の細波波及する、水夫長や航海士でさえある種の覚悟を決めて振り返れば、どういう気まぐれか、大海蛇、通りの向こうで動き止んで、鎌首をもたげて周囲の空気に何事か聞き入っているような。
lines.en:
Behind them came a predator none of the Albatross crew had ever heard of--except perhaps the chief engineer--a primeval hunter preserved into the present age by some malice of the creator. 
When it first appeared, it must still have been half asleep, for it now accelerated in pursuit. Ripples of despair spread through the ordinary sailors. Even the boatswain and navigators turned with grim resolve, only to see the great serpent halt capriciously at the far end of the street, raise its head, and seem to listen to something in the surrounding air.

lines.jp:
なんにせよ好機には違いなし、と、再び駆け出す皆だったが、誰もが気づいていた。
　自分達は、信天翁号が停泊する桟橋とは真逆の方向に走っている、と。
lines.en:
Whatever the reason, it was an opportunity, and everyone broke into another run. Yet they had all noticed the same thing. 
They were running in exactly the opposite direction from the pier where the Albatross was moored.

lines.jp:
やがて誰かが一つの建物を指差す、と船の上では珍しいくらいの一つ流れになってその扉に殺到していく。蹴り開けて、屋内の骨や有り合わせの防御壁を扉の内に築くが、あの劫初の恐怖相手ではどれほど保つものやら。
　この廃址ではどれも建物は似たり寄ったり、大海蛇への砦となるような堅固な建物はないだろうに、ここへ皆が逃げこんだのは、階を三階と重ね、周囲に比べて見晴らしが利いたからである。
lines.en:
Eventually someone pointed to a building, and in a display of unity rare aboard their ship, they all rushed its door. They kicked it open and piled bones and whatever else they could find into a barricade inside, though there was no telling how long it would hold against that primordial terror. 
The buildings in these ruins were all much alike, and none looked sturdy enough to serve as a fortress against the serpent. They chose this one only because it rose three stories and offered a better view than its neighbors.

lines.jp: 我先にと最上階に駆け上がって、皆窓へと飛びついた。
lines.en: Everyone raced one another to the top floor and threw themselves at the windows.

lines.jp: 「……どうだよ、朔屋」
lines.en: ...Well, Sakuya?

lines.jp: 「ぁー……、桟橋までの路に、がっちり居座っちまってますわ……」
lines.en: Uh... It's planted itself squarely on the road to the pier...

lines.jp: 運良くあの折り畳み式の望遠鏡を船から持ち出していた朔屋に観察役が命じられ、青年は観ているだけでなにやら不快な気分になる怪物を、いやいや望遠鏡で眺めるうちに、明らかになった事実は、あまり楽しいものではなかった。
lines.en: By good fortune, Naomasa had brought that collapsible telescope from the ship, so he was assigned to keep watch. He reluctantly studied the monster through the glass, though merely looking at it made him feel ill. What he learned was not encouraging.

lines.jp:
大海蛇は、廃址から桟橋を結ぶ、ただ一本の路に通ずる、木造の通りの合流点、ちょっとした広場様になっている地点にその長大な身体を留め、くねらせてあるという事。
　朔屋がそれを告げたところ。
lines.en:
The great sea serpent had stretched its long body across the small plaza where the wooden streets converged, controlling the only road that connected the ruins to the pier. 
When Naomasa reported this, someone replied,

lines.jp: 「つったってお前、何も馬鹿正直に路を通んなくちゃいけねえって法はねえわな。なんだったら屋根伝いに行ったっていいし、やりようは幾らでもあんだろ……」
lines.en: So what? There isn't any law saying we have to follow the road like honest fools. We could cross over the roofs if we had to. We've got plenty of options...

lines.jp: 「おう殺し屋。もう一回たたっ切ってこい」
lines.en: Hey, killer. Go cut it down one more time.

lines.jp: 「やんだおら。おめえ、ああやって用心棒の先生よろしく出て行ってよ、しくじった時のあのみっともなさったらねェぞ」
lines.en: Like hell. You go strutting out like some master swordsman hired to guard the place, then fail--you've no idea how damned humiliating that is.

lines.jp: 「もう二度とやりたくね」
lines.en: I'm never doing it again.

lines.jp: 斬れるか斬れないか、他人にどう思われたところでてんで構わぬ体の蒼眼居士、ただこっ恥ずかしかったのは本当のようで、吹かす煙管がせわしない。と、智里の視線がふいと流れた、先に。
lines.en: The blue-eyed swordsman cared nothing for whether he could cut the beast or what anyone else thought, but his embarrassment seemed genuine; he puffed restlessly at his pipe. Then Tomosato's gaze drifted toward something ahead.

lines.jp: 「無駄、だろうなあ」
lines.en: It would be pointless.

lines.jp:
こちらからせせら笑う事はあっても、嘲笑される事には血でもって酬いる信天翁号の水夫長と航海士が、殺気を漲らせて投げつけた視線の先、部屋の隅の丸椅子に座していたのは、あの老人だった。
　航海士二人にふざけた悪戯吹っかけ、下級水夫達を怯えさせ、そして、クロを錯乱するほどの恐怖に叩きこんだあの。
lines.en:
The boatswain and navigators of the Albatross freely mocked others, but repaid any ridicule directed at them with blood. Their murderous gazes fell upon the old man seated on a round stool in the corner of the room. 
The same old man who had played his outrageous prank on the two navigators, frightened the ordinary sailors, and plunged Kuro into terror so profound that she lost control of herself.

lines.jp: けくっ、と朔屋が聞いた奇妙な音は、クロが喉を引き攣らせた音。クロは朔屋の背後にしゃがみこみ、頭を抱えてがたがたと震えていた。老人は朔屋とクロには気づいた風もなく進み出て、窓から大海蛇を望見して、ひとしきり肩を震わせていたのは、声も無く笑っていたのだった───
lines.en: Naomasa heard a strange little choke: Kuro's throat had tightened. She crouched behind him, clutching her head and trembling violently. The old man showed no sign of noticing either her or Naomasa. He stepped forward, looked through the window at the great sea serpent, and shook his shoulders for some time. He was laughing soundlessly--

lines.jp: 「ありゃあな、あんな卑猥な頭をしておるが、この島に最後まで生き残って、そしてこれからも生き残り続けるだろうの、最悪の捕食動物だよ……」
lines.en: It may have an indecent-looking head, but that is the worst predator on this island--the one that survived to the very end, and will likely go on surviving.

lines.jp: 「ああいうなりをしとるが、その性、恐ろしく狡猾でなあ。あのあたりはほれ、この島の路の合流点であるし、雨が強く降れば水が溢れよる」
lines.en: Despite its appearance, its nature is terribly cunning. That place there is the junction of the island's roads, and when the rain grows heavy, it floods.

lines.jp: 「すれば、電気も通りやすくなるし、あいつはそんな事をせんでも鋭敏な感覚の持ち主でな」
lines.en: That makes electricity travel more easily. But even without it, the creature possesses exceedingly keen senses.

lines.jp: 「周囲三〇〇米くらいなら、生き物の生命電流を感じ取るよ。それで、どこまでも追いかけてきよるわ」
lines.en: It can detect the bioelectric currents of living creatures from roughly three hundred meters away. Once it does, it will pursue them anywhere.

lines.jp: 「一度狙われたら、まあ助からんな」
lines.en: Once it chooses you as prey, there is essentially no escape.

lines.jp:
「よく喋る爺だなあこいつあ！
　爺、やけにあの化け物に詳しいようじゃねえか。あんた、アレの飼い主かなんかか。
　だったらたたじゃおかねえ───」
lines.en:
You're a talkative old bastard! 
You seem to know an awful lot about that monster, old man. Are you its keeper or something? 
Because if you are, you won't get away with this--

lines.jp:
「そうとも、いう。
　儂がこの島に、全ての生き物を持ちこんだんだからな。当然、あれもだ」
lines.en:
You might say that. 
After all, I brought every living creature to this island. That one included, naturally.
Old man...

lines.jp: 「爺ではない。儂の名は、ノアという」
lines.en: Not 'old man.' My name is Noah.

lines.jp:
「ホ！　ノアと来やがったか！　爺、てめえにゃ随分過ぎた名だなぁ！
　それともご先祖様かなんかかあんたの」
lines.en:
Ha! Noah, is it? That's a grand name for the likes of you! 
Or was it some ancestor's name?

lines.jp: 「聖人にかぶれて、てめぇの餓鬼に同じ名をつける奴があるが、あんたの親もその口か」
lines.en: Some people get carried away with saints and give their children the same names. Were your parents that sort?

lines.jp: 水夫長の揶揄は一同の意気を鼓舞する為で、言わば老人は槍玉に挙げられたわけだが、返ってきたのは意想外の反撃の、水夫長は老練な眼を困惑に白黒させたという。
lines.en: The boatswain's taunts were meant to rally everyone's spirits, making the old man a convenient target. But the unexpected counterattack left even that seasoned brute blinking in bewilderment.

lines.jp: 「だから、儂がそのノアだ、と言うておるのよ。本人様じゃい、その人じゃい、ｅｃｃｅ　ｈｏｍｏじゃい」
lines.en: I am telling you that I am that Noah. The man himself. Behold the man: ecce homo.

lines.jp:
───たとえ聖書の名を知らない人間であっても、『ノアの方舟』の名は知っていようと言うくらい有名な、伝説中の伝説だ。
　旧約聖書の巻頭を飾る「創世記」において、ノアの方舟伝説が登場するのは第六章。
　……ちなみにアダムとイヴが楽園を追放されたのが第三章。この楽園追放をもって人類の繁栄は始まる訳だから、間二章しか保たずに人類は破滅の時を迎える事になる。まあ信天翁号の面子を見ていると、大概の神ならそれを考えるようになるだろうが。
lines.en:
Even people unfamiliar with the Bible have generally heard the name "Noah's Ark." It is one of the world's most famous legends. 
The account of Noah's Ark appears in chapter six of Genesis, the first book of the Old Testament. 
Incidentally, Adam and Eve were expelled from Paradise in chapter three. Since humanity's prosperity began with that expulsion, it took only two intervening chapters for the species to reach the brink of destruction. Looking at the crew of the Albatross, one could understand why most gods would contemplate the same solution.

lines.jp:
さて、アダムとイヴの子孫たる人類が、産めよ殖やせと地に満ちて大いなる繁栄を享受するも、まあその素行の悪さにいたくお怒りになった神が手による、四〇日間にわたる暴風雨と大洪水に襲われ、地上の万物は悉く水に没し去った。
　ただ一つの生き残り、生命の最後の希望は、神が『善きひと』と認定したノアとその家族、彼らが造った方舟と、それに集められた雄雌一番いずつの動物たちだけ、なんとも心細い限りである。
lines.en:
The descendants of Adam and Eve multiplied, filled the earth, and enjoyed great prosperity. But their conduct so enraged God that He sent forty days of storm and a great flood, submerging all things upon the earth. 
The only survivors, the final hope of life, were Noah, whom God had judged a righteous man, Noah's family, the ark they built, and one male and female of every animal gathered aboard it--a desperately fragile hope.

lines.jp: 結局大水は一五〇日もの間地の面を没させ、減じていくまでが更に一五〇日の期間を要したという。七月の一七日にアララテ山の頂上に漂着した方舟の中から、ノアは鳩を放ち水の引き具合を確かめようとするが、水はなお大地を満たして、鳩の留まれるような物や場所はなにもなく、鳩はノアの元へ空しく帰還した。七日後、再び放った鳩は橄欖の若葉を加えて戻り、水が引きつつある事を告げ、更に七日後に放つともう再び船には戻らなかった……落ち着くべき陸地を発見していたからである。
lines.en: The flood covered the earth for one hundred and fifty days, and took another one hundred and fifty to subside. After the ark came to rest upon the mountains of Ararat on the seventeenth day of the seventh month, Noah released a dove to learn whether the waters had withdrawn. But water still covered the earth, leaving it nowhere to perch, and it returned to him empty-handed. Seven days later he released the dove again; it returned with a young olive leaf, showing that the waters were receding. Released once more after another seven days, it did not return, having found dry land on which to settle.

lines.jp: かくして『西暦』なら六〇〇と一年の二月二七日に、神の啓示によってノアと家族は船を出で、地上には再び生き物による真の繁栄が築かれた、つまり現在の世界に存在する生き物というのは皆このノアと方舟に乗り合わせていた物達の子孫と言う事になる……。
lines.en: Thus, on the twenty-seventh day of the second month in the six hundred and first year, Noah and his family left the ark at God's command. True prosperity among living creatures was established once again upon the earth. In other words, every living thing in the present world descends from Noah and the creatures that shared his ark...

lines.jp:
これが世に伝わる『ノアの方舟と大洪水』伝説のあらましではあるが。
　皆、居合わせた者一同、ノアを名乗った老人を源に生じ濃さと暗さを増しながら、じわりじわりと迫る、言わば古よりの影に肩や胸元を押されるような圧迫感に押し黙った、訳ではない。
　自分が伝説中の登場人物その人である、と告げられたところで、別に信天翁号の面子ならずとて、はいそうですかと納得できるようなものでもあるまい。なるほど、この島は明らかに異様で、島内には確かに、多種多様の生物たちの番の骨が散乱している。
　島内全体の木造建築物にも、どれもこれも古さが画一化されている、得体の知れ無さが立ち籠めている。
lines.en:
That is the outline of the legend known to the world as "Noah's Ark and the Great Flood." 
Yet everyone present did not fall silent because some ancient shadow, flowing from the old man who called himself Noah, seemed to deepen and press slowly against their shoulders and chests. 
The crew of the Albatross--or anyone else, for that matter--could hardly be expected to accept a man's claim that he was a figure from legend. Certainly this island was plainly unnatural, and pairs of bones from all manner of creatures did lie scattered across it. 
Every wooden structure on the island also possessed the same uniform age, lending the entire place an inscrutable air.

lines.jp:
けれど、だからといって、ここでたとえ老人がノアを名乗ったとしても『方舟伝説』を思わせる程の太古からの、怖るべき、遙けき時間の堆積までは感じられない、というのが船員達の正直な印象であり、加えてそもそもの矛盾が生じている。
　水夫長が、老人を自前の鷲のような目と、刺青の龍で睨み据えながら、ばん、と室内の壁にプレス機の如き勢いで掌叩きつければ、彼の内心の苛立ち示すようにもうもうと埃舞い上がり、下級水夫君達を咳きこませる。
lines.en:
Even so, the old man's claim to be Noah did not convey the terrifying weight of ages that the legend of the ark implied. That was the crew's honest impression. Besides, his story contained a fundamental contradiction. 
The boatswain fixed the old man beneath his eagle-like eyes and the glare of his dragon tattoo, then slammed a palm against the wall with the force of a press. Dust billowed up as if displaying his irritation and sent the young sailors into fits of coughing.

lines.jp:
「百歩譲っててめえが本物のノアで、くたばり損なってここにいるとしよう。
　なら、なんで俺達はここにいるんだよっ」
lines.en:
Suppose, just for the sake of argument, that you're the real Noah and somehow failed to die all this time. 
Then why the hell are we here?

lines.jp:
「それに世界の生き物も、あんたの方舟の生き物たちの子孫なんだろみんな！
　それがここで骨になってちゃあ、子孫もクソもねえやあ！」
lines.en:
And every creature in the world is supposed to descend from the animals on your ark! 
If they're all bones here, they couldn't have any damned descendants!

lines.jp: ……わざわざ相手の言葉に乗った上で、それを論理で打ち負かそうとするとはこの強面の男も案外律儀者だが、一方老人はまた窓から大海蛇の様子を眺め、頭巾の裡でほくそ笑んで肩を震わせる様は、出来のいい兵器を愛でる死の商人のようですらあり、とうてい全ての生き物を後世に伝える事許された『善き人』とは思えなかったが、
lines.en: The fierce-looking man was unexpectedly conscientious, going so far as to accept the other's premise before trying to defeat it logically. Meanwhile, the old man peered through the window at the serpent again and chuckled beneath his hood, his shoulders shaking. He looked like an arms dealer admiring a particularly fine weapon, hardly the righteous man entrusted with carrying all living things into the future.

lines.jp:
「ノアが一人だけだなどと誰が決めたんじゃ。
　一文明の崩壊にあたって、当時現存しておる生物相の保存管理役に当てられた者は、皆ノアじゃ」
lines.en:
Who decided there was only one Noah? 
Whenever a civilization collapsed, everyone assigned to preserve and manage the surviving biosphere was a Noah.

lines.jp:
「は……はぁん？
　てめえ、なに言って……」
lines.en:
Wh... what? 
What the hell are you talking about...?

lines.jp: 「だいたい、生物相を保存しようという大難事、一つの計画、一つの作戦だけに頼る訳なかろ。お前達だとて、重要な計画にはフォローちうのをつけるだろうが」
lines.en: The preservation of an entire biosphere was far too difficult a task to entrust to a single plan or operation. Even you people provide what you call a fallback for an important undertaking, do you not?

lines.jp: 「儂はな、第三次『方舟計画』プランβ、ウリエルタイプのプロジェクトマスター、コードネーム『ノア』、認識番号００００四－二三甲、本名……は、この際どうでもええわ」
lines.en: I was project master of Plan Beta, Uriel type, under the Third Ark Project. Codename: Noah. Identification number: 00004-23A. My true name... is unimportant now.

lines.jp: とうとうと、立て板に水、というより油でも流すかの流暢さで捲し立てられても、一同には異次元の言語でも駆使されているようにとんと理解が及ばず───だが、老人はそこまで語ったものの。肩を落とした、ようにしか見えなかった。
lines.en: He rattled it off with the fluency of oil, not merely water, poured down a standing board, but to the crew he might as well have been speaking a language from another dimension. They understood none of it. Yet when the old man had said his piece, his shoulders seemed to fall.

lines.jp:
「しかし儂は……果たせンかった。
　他のノア達は……どうなったか知らん。
　なんにせよ、儂の方舟はいつまで経っても」
lines.en:
But I... failed. 
I do not know what happened to the other Noahs. 
Whatever the case, my ark never...

lines.jp: 「───嵐から、抜けられんかったよ」
lines.en: --Never escaped the storm.

lines.jp:
窓辺から離れ、室内を歩み、また丸椅子に戻って座すまで、数歩の間、その僅かな間に老人から、長衣の肩やその内側から、救いようのないほど倦み疲れた者の悲哀と、生涯を捧げた計画の頓挫を迎えた者の、凄惨な絶望とが溢れだし、部屋を濃い翳りに塗り替えてくいかのよう。
　椅子に腰を下ろしたすがたにも、重荷に耐えかねた人の拭い去りがたい疲労が澱んでひたすらに沈鬱だった。
lines.en:
He left the window and crossed the room to sit again on the round stool. In those few steps--that briefest span--sorrow spilled from his shoulders and from within his robe: the grief of one exhausted beyond all hope, and the harrowing despair of someone whose life's work had ended in failure. It seemed to repaint the room in dense shadow. 
Even after he sat, the indelible weariness of one crushed beneath a burden pooled around him, unrelieved and bleak.

lines.jp:
「なにが原因なのか、いまだもって不明だ。
　気象制御システムがこのような誤動作を起こす事など、セキュリテイ上ありえん。時空閉鎖系も方舟計画の船には干渉権限を保持しない」
lines.en:
Even now, the cause remains unknown. 
The weather-control system could not possibly have malfunctioned in this fashion under its security design. Nor did the closed spacetime system retain authority to interfere with vessels of the Ark Project.

lines.jp: 「だが事実として嵐は儂の方舟を襲い続けた……いや、襲い続けている。今もだ。お前たちも知るとおりだ。船は、いまだ嵐に囚われたままだよ」
lines.en: Yet the storm continued to assail my ark... No, it continues still. Even now. As you yourselves know, the vessel remains trapped within the storm.

lines.jp:
「物語の復元能力が働いたのではないか。
　儂はそう睨んでおる。なにしろ、生物相を保存する、という題目の下、当時は現存しておらなんだモノまで収集したからな」
lines.en:
Perhaps the restorative power of narrative took effect. 
That is my suspicion. Under the stated purpose of preserving the biosphere, we collected even things that no longer existed at the time.

lines.jp: 「どこかに無理をかければ、どこかにその歪みが来る。……ま、当然の道理だわ」
lines.en: Strain one part of the world, and the distortion emerges elsewhere. A perfectly natural principle.

lines.jp: 次第に老人の声が低く成りゆき、廃屋に積もった埃の中に吸われていったが、その物哀しさは哀しさとして、どうにもおかしな点がちらほらと。そもそも老人が使う語句からして意味不明ではあったが、そればかりではない。石鹸の、虹色に色合いを転変させる泡の中に、幾つか濁った物が混ざるのを見て、老人に問いかける。
lines.en: The old man's voice gradually sank until the dust piled through the abandoned house seemed to absorb it. His sorrow remained sorrow, but several things still felt wrong. The terms he used were incomprehensible to begin with, and that was not all. As though noticing muddy blemishes within an iridescent soap bubble, Naomasa questioned him.

lines.jp: 「爺さんの言ってる事はさっぱりわかんないけどさ。じゃあまあそっちはそっちとして、爺さんのその方舟とやらはどこよ？　まだこの嵐ン中から出られてないんだろ？」
lines.en: I don't understand a thing you're saying, old man. But setting all that aside, where is this ark of yours? It still hasn't escaped the storm, right?

lines.jp: 朔屋の問いに航海士が何事か口にしかけたが、結局はなにも言わずに押し黙る、言うのが面倒になっただけかも知れぬ。
lines.en: One of the navigators began to say something in response to Naomasa's question, then thought better of it and remained silent. Perhaps she simply found it too much trouble.

lines.jp: 「どこ、もなにも。こういう時にも、察しの悪い奴というのはどうしても一人は混じるもんだな……若造、この島がそうだ」
lines.en: Where? There is always at least one dull-witted person in a group at moments like this... Young man, this island is the ark.

lines.jp: 丸椅子に身を起こし、片腕をさ、横に伸ばして凪ぐ仕草、島全体示すように。
lines.en: Rising from his stool, he extended one arm sideways and swept it across the air, as though indicating the island in its entirety.

lines.jp: 「この島は、儂の方舟を解体して造ったんだ、と、ここまで聞けば大概判りそうなもんだがな」
lines.en: I dismantled my ark and used it to build this island. Most people would have worked that out from what I have already told you.

lines.jp:
───現在彼らが隠れるこの三階建ての廃屋、そしてその他全ての廃屋、島内を走る通路、各構造物、ばかりか恐らくこの島全てが、『ノアの方舟』を解体して、その構造材で組み上げた───と言われても、一同にはやはり実感に乏しい話としか。
　この島が一つの木造建築物である。ここまではいい。シサム・キサラもそれは感じ取っている。それ自体は大いなる驚異だ。
　が、しかし、それが元は一つの船だった、と告げられても、まるで実感が生じない、と言うのが一同の正直な印象であった。
　そもそも信天翁号の一向は、老人がノアその人だと名乗った時点で、ボケが高じたあげく妄言を吐くようになった徘徊老人、程度にしか考えていない。
lines.en:
The three-story ruin where they now hid, every other abandoned building, the passages across the island, each structure--and probably the entire island itself--had supposedly been assembled from the dismantled timbers of Noah's Ark. Still, the crew found the story difficult to grasp. 
The island was a single wooden construction. That much they could accept; both Sisam and Kisara had sensed it, and the fact was astounding in its own right. 
But being told that the whole thing had once been a single ship inspired no feeling of reality in any of them. 
Besides, from the moment the old man called himself Noah, the Albatross crew had regarded him as little more than a senile wanderer whose decline had progressed into delusion.

lines.jp:
「え……じゃあ、方舟ばらしちゃったの？　
　はー。そらまあさぞやご苦労な。
　……ん？　ああ、判った判ったクロ、
　もうこの爺さんとは口、聞かねえから」
lines.en:
What...? So you took the ark apart? 
Wow. That must've been a lot of work. 
...Hm? Fine, fine, Kuro, I understand. 
I won't talk to this old man anymore.

lines.jp:
老人の登場時より怯えきっているクロは、朔屋が彼に話しかけただけでもいよいよ狂乱の度合い深め、青年の背で縮み上がってはぐいぐいと、とにかく老人から隠れたい離れたい一心で、朔屋を引っ張る朔屋の背に顔を押しつける。
　少しばかり扱いあぐね、背後に手を回して軽く頭を撫でてやるのがせいぜいの、皆でこうして逃れてきたところを自分達だけ離れる訳にもいくまい。そうやって離れてしまうのも危険なような気もするし。
lines.en:
Kuro had been terrified since the old man's arrival. Merely hearing Naomasa speak to him drove her closer to frenzy. She shrank against his back, tugging him while pressing her face into him, wanting only to hide from the old man and get away. 
Naomasa had no idea how to handle her beyond reaching back to pat her head gently. They could hardly separate from everyone else after fleeing here together, and leaving the group felt dangerous in its own right.

lines.jp: 「もちろん儂とて『方舟』を解体などしたくはなかった……どれだけ台風が続こうとも……理論的には、大型級で風速七〇ノット級の台風に常時晒され続けても、五世紀は無補給無整備で持ちこたえられる……そのように設計、建造されておったしな……」
lines.en: Naturally, I did not wish to dismantle the ark... No matter how long the typhoon continued... In theory, it was designed and built to endure constant exposure to a major typhoon with winds of seventy knots for five centuries, without resupply or maintenance...

lines.jp: 「航海当初は全てが順調にいっておった。食料、水、薬品の備蓄は十二分にあり、給餌装置も、排泄物の処理装置も、捕食生物、攻撃性の強い生物の情動抑制装置も。皆問題なく稼働しておったよ……しかし」
lines.en: At the beginning of the voyage, everything proceeded smoothly. We had more than ample reserves of food, water, and medicine. The feeding equipment, waste-treatment equipment, and emotion-suppression systems for predators and highly aggressive creatures all functioned without difficulty... But then...

lines.jp:
───ある日。
　───悲劇が起こったのだ、という。
　──動力供給機構の異常動作、そして停止だったと老人は語った。
lines.en:
--Then one day.
 --Tragedy struck.
 The power-supply system malfunctioned, the old man said--and stopped.

lines.jp: 凶暴な攻撃本能を持つ生物たちを抑制していた機構も、動力の供給が止まってしまえば廃物と変わりない。水夫長が発見したような太古の生物中の覇者、暴君、それに航海士も語ったように猫科の捕食者達。他にも見当もつかないような生物もあったかも知れない───そう、今一行の死神となっているあの大海蛇といった───
lines.en: Once the power supply failed, the systems restraining creatures with violent predatory instincts became useless. There were the rulers and tyrants among primordial beasts like the one the boatswain had found, and the feline predators the navigators described. There might have been other unimaginable creatures as well--such as the very great sea serpent now serving as the crew's executioner.

lines.jp:
……動力供給機構の復旧まで三日三晩の連続作業が要求されたというし、結局完全なる修復は不可能だったのだという。
　その間に事態は悪化の一途を迎え、穏和な生き物たちは次々と捕食者達の牙にかかり、清掃、空調の両装置の作動不能が遺体の腐敗とそれに端を発する疫病の蔓延を招いた。
　そして、嵐───予定されていた四〇日を過ぎても全く収まる兆しもなく吹き荒れ続ける嵐。船内の人間、管理者達は絶望した。
lines.en:
...Restoring the power system supposedly required three days and nights of uninterrupted work, and even then a complete repair proved impossible. 
In the meantime, conditions only worsened. Docile creatures fell one after another to the predators' fangs. With the cleaning and ventilation systems disabled, corpses decayed and disease spread in their wake. 
And there was the storm--the storm that continued to rage without the slightest sign of abating even after its scheduled forty days had passed. The humans aboard, the ark's administrators, despaired.

lines.jp: ……朔屋は想像してみる。むっとする閉じきった世界。広さは、とりあえずタンカーくらいだろうか。その内部は暗闇に閉ざされ、船内の機械は全てまともに動かない。そんな暗闇の中を徘徊し、手当たり次第に他の生物に襲いかかる猛獣たち。蔓延する死の気配に疫病───間違いなく自分であれば精神が保たない。一晩目でたやすく発狂するだろう。
lines.en: ...Naomasa tried to imagine it: a stifling, enclosed world, perhaps the size of a tanker. Darkness sealed the interior, and none of the ship's machinery worked properly. Savage beasts roamed that darkness, attacking every living thing they encountered. The presence of death everywhere, disease spreading... Naomasa knew without question that his mind would not endure it. He would go mad on the very first night.

lines.jp:
「全体の機構はある程度復興したが、それでも十全とはとうてい言えず、うち続く嵐……。
　船は堅牢であったが、人間の精神の方が保たなんだな。儂や他の管理者達はまだ耐えられた事態でも、家族達は別だった」
lines.en:
We restored the overall system to some extent, but it remained far from fully functional, and the storm continued without end... 
The ship was strong, but the human mind was not. The other administrators and I could endure circumstances that our families could not.

lines.jp: 「……同僚、というよりあれは、儂にとっては弟のような男がおってな……そいつも死んだよ。船内を哨戒中、オオアリクイに背後から襲いかかられ、ふりほどく事もできずその舌を鼻孔から差し入れられ、脳髄を全て啜らりとられてな……」
lines.en: ...I had a colleague--no, he was like a younger brother to me. He died too. While patrolling the ship, a giant anteater attacked him from behind. He could not shake it off, and it thrust its tongue through his nostril and consumed his entire brain...

lines.jp:
「彼の妻はその時臨月だった……彼の死が伝わってしもうてな。ショックで異常出産を起こし、子供も母胎も保たんかった。
　今際のきわに哀願されたよ。
　───どうか、生き物たちに陸地を───
　と。自分や夫、そして子供が死ぬ事よりも、最期まで生き物達の末を憂いておったわい」
lines.en:
His wife was in the final month of pregnancy... News of his death reached her. The shock brought on a catastrophic labor, and neither mother nor child survived. 
At the very end, she begged something of me. 
--Please, give the creatures dry land--
Even as she, her husband, and her child died, she worried to her last breath about the fate of the animals.

lines.jp: ……辛気くさい話だ、と水夫長以下欠伸を垂れたのが信天翁号面子である。ちなみに朔屋はついうっかりもらい泣きをしていたりで。
lines.en: ...What a depressing story, thought the crew of the Albatross, from the boatswain down, and they yawned. Naomasa, incidentally, had accidentally begun to cry along with him.

lines.jp:
「それで儂も、心が決まった。
　とにかく、仮初めでいい、こんな密閉された船内でない、島を造ろうと」
lines.en:
That was when I made my decision. 
No matter how temporary, I would build an island--somewhere that was not the interior of a sealed ship.

lines.jp:
「まあ困難は当然あった訳だが、結果としてはお前たちが乗っかっているこの島だ。
　島を築き、島内に生き物たちを養う為の家屋を築き───それでも雨は、やはり降りやまんかった」
lines.en:
Naturally, the undertaking posed difficulties, but the result is the island beneath your feet. 
I built the island, and upon it buildings to shelter the creatures--yet the rain still would not cease.

lines.jp: 老人の声が、熱望と絶望、そして渇望とが渦巻いて、どろどろと滾るような内圧を秘めゆき、室内の床を這うように広がっては満ちて、一行は老人を核として部屋が暗く翳りゆくかの心地に囚われた。
lines.en: Longing, despair, and desperate craving swirled within the old man's voice, gathering a molten inner pressure. It spread across the floor and filled the room, until the crew felt the chamber itself darkening around the old man at its center.

lines.jp:
「儂は必死で鳥を放ち続けたよ。
　陸地の証を持ち帰る事をひたすら念じてな。
　何度も───何度も。
　ひたすらの祈りと共に───」
lines.en:
I desperately continued releasing birds. 
Each time, I prayed only that it would return bearing proof of dry land. 
Again--and again. 
Always accompanied by the same prayer--

lines.jp: ゆっくり立ち上がる老人は、人と言うより、長衣の中に執念と妄執をガス状に詰め込んで、過去が伸ばしてきた手のように思え、歩む動きもどこか関節や靱帯の構造が勝手の異なるように、くにゃくにゃと、そう見えるほど、緩慢で音のない動きだったのに。
lines.en: The old man slowly stood. He seemed less a human being than a hand extended by the past, his long robe filled with gaseous obsession and fixation. Though his movements were slow and soundless, they looked strangely boneless, as though the joints and ligaments beneath obeyed some other design.

lines.jp: どすん、と音は朔屋の背後から。ばたばたともがく音も続いて、見ればクロは、声さえ出せないくらいに必死で引きつった形相で、老人から逃げだそうとあがいており、なのに恐慌のあまり手足に意味のある動き、全く宿らず。
lines.en: A heavy thump came from behind Naomasa, followed by frantic struggling. Kuro's face was twisted in such desperate terror that she could not even make a sound. She fought to escape the old man, but panic had stripped every purposeful movement from her limbs.

lines.jp:
老人が進む───
　クロが引きつる。
　
　老人が歩む───
　
　クロが隠れる場所を求めて頭を振り回す。
　老人が手を伸ばす───
lines.en:
The old man advanced--
Kuro's body drew taut. 

The old man walked--

Kuro whipped her head about, searching for somewhere to hide. 
The old man reached out--

lines.jp: クロの喉が過呼吸を起こし、冬枯れの風の音を鳴らす。朔屋が飛びついて背後に庇う。
lines.en: Kuro began to hyperventilate, her throat making the sound of wind through dead winter branches. Naomasa lunged over and shielded her behind him.

lines.jp: 「おい爺さん、なにちっちゃい女の子を脅かしてんだ。ほら見ろ、こんなになって。まだ漏らしてないのが不思議なくらいで───」
lines.en: Hey, old man! Why are you terrorizing a little girl? Look at her. It's a wonder she hasn't wet herself yet--

lines.jp:
「なにが……女の子だ……。
　儂が放ったのは、鴉よ。
　艶やかで黒き、そして強い羽根。
　嵐にも負けぬ……な」
lines.en:
What... little girl? 
The bird I released was a raven. 
Glossy black feathers, strong feathers. 
Feathers that would not yield even to the storm...

lines.jp:
「鳥の中の鳥、その叡智は神話中の常連となるほどの、な。
　これ以上に使命を託すに相応しい鳥が、他にあろうか」
lines.en:
The greatest of birds, whose wisdom has earned it a place throughout mythology. 
What bird could have been more worthy of the mission?

lines.jp:
「だから儂は、全ての船員、生き物の為に願いを込めて、鴉を放ち続けた。
　陸地を発見させる為になぁ……」
lines.en:
And so, carrying the hopes of every crew member and every creature, I released the raven again and again. 
I sent it to discover dry land...

lines.jp:
「だがその鴉は何度放っても戻ってきよる。陸を見つけもせんでな。
　儂は呪った。その艶やかな黒。
　大いなる叡智の色、黒」
lines.en:
Yet no matter how many times I released it, the raven returned without finding land. 
I cursed that lustrous black. 
Black, the color of profound wisdom.

lines.jp: 老人が、朔屋の前に立つ。朔屋の鼻先に漂う、黴臭さ、幽かな腐臭、薬品臭さ、オイルの匂い、それらが青年に、目の前に立つものを人と言うよりも、長衣の形をした何かの機械とか、研究室とかそんなものを連想させ、たじろいだ瞬間に肩に掛かった手、さしたる剛力にもあらず、なのに手首の一返しで青年は部屋の隅まで放り出されるが薄汚れて片方しかない靴下のよう、無用、邪魔、それ以外の何ものでもないと。
lines.en: The old man stopped before Naomasa. Mustiness, faint decay, chemicals, and oil drifted under the young man's nose, suggesting that the thing before him was not a person so much as a machine or laboratory shaped like a robe. As Naomasa recoiled, a hand landed on his shoulder. It possessed no remarkable strength, yet a single turn of its wrist flung him into the corner like one filthy, unmatched sock: useless, obstructive, and nothing more.

lines.jp:
そして青年がのけられれば白、この時の白は、溶け崩れた乳酪のように床に頽れ、びくり、びくりと身を震わせるばかりで、手足は完全に萎えていた。
　そもそもクロが、四肢の使いようからして頼りないのも当然だったのだ。本来あるべき形ではなかったのだから。
lines.en:
With the young man swept aside, there lay white. White collapsed across the floor like curdling, melting cheese, able only to twitch and shudder, every limb gone limp.
 Of course Kuro had always seemed uncertain even in the use of her arms and legs. This was not the shape she was meant to have.

lines.jp:
「……全く役に立たなかったではないか！
　だから。儂は！　呪ってやったわい。
　役立たずの鴉を」
lines.en:
You were utterly useless! 
And so I--I cursed you! 
I cursed the worthless raven!

lines.jp:
「陸地を見つけるその時まで、休む事ならじ、戻ってくる事ならじ、と。
　そうそう、ついでにな、他の鴉と区別がつくように───」
lines.en:
Until you find dry land, you shall never rest and never return. 
Oh yes, and so that I could distinguish you from the other ravens--

lines.jp: 「呪って、みぃんな、白くしてヤッたわい」
lines.en: I cursed every last one of you white.

lines.jp: ノアが、身を二つ折りにする、その挙動は圧搾空気で動かす人形のよう、しかもクロを脅かす為にわざとやっているような節すら見受けられ、老人の本性の歪みを物語る。
lines.en: Noah folded himself in half, moving like a doll driven by compressed air. There was even a hint that he deliberately exaggerated the motion to frighten Kuro, revealing the distortion at the heart of his nature.

lines.jp: 「おうおう、そこにいるわ。かつての力全てを失った、哀れで、みじめで、誰からも望まれぬ、そんな情けない生き物が」
lines.en: Oh yes, there it is. A pitiful, wretched creature that has lost every power it once possessed and is wanted by no one.

lines.jp: 「かつての面影など無いくせに、名前だけは未だ名乗っているのが滑稽でならんわ！」
lines.en: It retains nothing of its former glory, yet still goes by the same name. How laughable!

lines.jp: クロは……まず視線が上にくるりとぶれた。喪神の霧の中に逃げ込もうとしたようだがそんな都合のいい逃避を老人は許さず、むしろこちらの方が意地悪鳥の鉤爪のような指の先を伸ばし、少女のあばらをたっぷりとくすぐっては、恐怖に笑い声も出ない、痙攣的な笑いでこちらに引き戻し、赤い眸、今は血が滲んだような濁りきった眸を覗きこんで、たっぷりと怯えの味を賞味してから。
lines.en: Kuro's gaze first rolled upward, as though she meant to escape into the fog of unconsciousness. The old man denied her even that convenient refuge. He extended fingers like the claws of a malicious bird and tickled fiercely along her ribs, dragging her back with silent, convulsive laughter born of terror. He peered into her red eyes, now clouded as if blood had seeped through them, and savored her fear at length.

lines.jp: 「クロ……烏などと───っ」
lines.en: To call yourself Kuro... a raven--

lines.jp:
「……ｋｅっ……、
　ｋｅっ、ｋａ───
　ｋａａａａａｈｈｈｈｈっ！」
lines.en:
...Keh... 
Keh, ka--
Kaaaaaahhhhhh!

lines.jp: 皆思わず耳を塞いだ。それくらい聞き苦しく不快で惨めな悲鳴だった。人間の声ですらなかった。思えばクロが舌足らずだったのも当然で、元々が人の言葉を喋るような生き物ではない。かといって今更本来の音で啼こうにも、その喉は人のもの、鳥の声艶やかに長く伸ばすようには造られておらず、クロはどちらの声、言葉であろうと不自由でしかないのだろう。クロ、ミュルメコレオンの悲哀を宿すもの。
lines.en: Everyone instinctively covered their ears. The scream was that grating, wretched, and miserable. It was not even a human voice. In retrospect, Kuro's halting speech was only natural: she had never been a creature meant to speak human language. Yet when she tried now to cry in her first voice, her throat was human, not made to sustain the rich, ringing call of a bird. In either voice, in either language, Kuro could express herself only imperfectly. Kuro, bearing the sorrow of the myrmecoleon.

lines.jp:
啼いて、いやいやをして、涙を撒き散らして、息もできなくて、咳きこんで、悶えて、逃げようとして体をぶつけて、ここまで哀れな姿を、誰も手を貸そうというものはいなくて、というより呆気にとられていた。
　老人の話など与太半分に聞いていた上に、信天翁号の嵐を呼ぶ船長、といえば勇ましいが、嵐の時以外はてんで役に立たない少女を捕まえて、強い羽根だの偉大な知恵だの鴉だの。老人の頭がいよいよトチ狂ったのではないかとやや引き気味に見たのも、仕方ない事だろう。
lines.en:
She cried, shook her head, scattered tears, failed to breathe, coughed, writhed, and battered herself against things in her attempts to escape. Yet no one offered to help her in this pitiable state. More accurately, everyone stood dumbfounded. 
They had only half believed the old man's story. And though calling Kuro the storm-summoning captain of the Albatross sounded impressive, outside a storm she was a thoroughly helpless girl. To hear him speak of strong feathers, great wisdom, and ravens made them wonder, with some discomfort, whether the old man had finally gone completely mad.

lines.jp: ようやくショックから立ち上がった朔屋が、クロを老人から引き離してやれば、その手に縋りつく、非力な手のいとおしさ。頭を胸にかき抱いて、
lines.en: At last Naomasa recovered from the shock and pulled Kuro away from the old man. Her weak hands clung to his with heartrending desperation. He gathered her head against his chest.

lines.jp: 「ひでぇ……それ、全然クロのせいじゃないだろうが……」
lines.en: That's horrible... None of that was Kuro's fault...

lines.jp: 朔屋でさえ指摘できる論理の綻びを、しかし老人は平然と受けて流した、別のパラダイムで、それは神話、伝承の拠って立つところのもので。
lines.en: Even Naomasa could point out the flaw in that logic. Yet the old man calmly deflected it with a different paradigm: the principles upon which myth and legend rested.

lines.jp: 「いいや。その鴉のせいだな。神話・伝説の再構築には、遵守しなければならない事柄、順序といったものが存在する」
lines.en: No. It was the raven's fault. The reconstruction of a myth or legend has requirements and an order that must be observed.

lines.jp:
「そういった手順を踏まねば、記録は物語に、そして伝説には昇華し得ないのでな。
　儂の物語では、鳥が陸の証を持ち帰ることがなにより重要だった……」
lines.en:
Unless those steps are followed, a record cannot be sublimated into a story, and then a legend. 
In my story, it was essential above all else that a bird return bearing proof of land...

lines.jp: ノアが放ち続けた鳥───鴉。
lines.en: The bird Noah released again and again--a raven.

lines.jp:
その鴉こそが、クロの正体。
　クロのクロウは、鴉のクロウ。
lines.en:
That raven was Kuro's true identity. 
The "crow" in Kuro was crow indeed.

lines.jp: 「お前は───陸地にたどり着けたのか？　儂らの至るべき、陸を───」
lines.en: Did you--did you reach dry land? The land toward which we were meant to sail--
O raven--

lines.jp: 真剣に、黒々とした渇望一色で塗りつぶし、語りかける老人を見ても、他の面子はやはり、信じられないでいたのだけれど、この時、クロの髪に変容が、朔屋が一度目にしたあの変容が、また生じていた。
lines.en: Even faced with the old man speaking in deadly earnest, his entire being painted in black longing, the others still could not believe him. But then Kuro's hair underwent the same change Naomasa had witnessed once before.

lines.jp:
白い髪の中に浮いたのは小さな黒の斑。
　見やる間に小指の先から短冊や小皿くらいの大きさに拡大し、数も二つ・三つ・四つとどんどん増えて後はもう数え果たさず。どんどん浮いて、だんだらに染まっていく。白の中に黒が、浮かび上がって。
lines.en:
A small black spot appeared amid the white hair. 
As they watched, it grew from the tip of a little finger to the size of a paper strip, then a small plate. Two, three, four spots appeared, multiplying until they could no longer be counted. More and more rose to the surface, staining the white in uneven patches of black.

lines.jp:
「ク、クロ……っ。
　見つけた。知ってる。たくさん。
　だから、だからもう許して」
lines.en:
K-Kuro... 
Kuro found it. Kuro knows. So many. 
So, please... Please forgive Kuro now.

lines.jp:
その黒い色合い自体は、最上の漆や黒蜜を思わせてとても綺麗ではあったけれども。
　それが斑に白の中に散らかって、出鱈目な模様に染め抜いている様子は、お世辞にも綺麗とは言えず、それどころか奇病の症例のように見えた。
　信天翁号の船員達は、それまでクロがそのような変容を見せるなど知らず、この一時で老人の言葉が必ずしも絵空事ばかりではないのではないかと考え始めたのである。
lines.en:
The black itself was beautiful, reminiscent of the finest lacquer or dark molasses. 
But scattered in patches across the white, staining it in a random pattern, it could not honestly be called lovely. If anything, it resembled the symptoms of a bizarre disease. 
The sailors of the Albatross had never known Kuro could undergo such a transformation. In that moment, they began to wonder whether the old man's words might not be entirely fantasy.

lines.jp: 「クロの呪い、といて───！」
lines.en: Break Kuro's curse--!

lines.jp: 老人に縋りつこうとするも、触れられるのも厭だと言わんばかりにノアは、クロの額を手で押し返すものだから、白子の少女の脚ばかりが空しく床を掻く、それでも少女は何度でも縋ろうとする、今の自分をこうしてしまったのが老人なら、哀願するしかないではないか、と。
lines.en: She tried to cling to the old man, but Noah pushed against her forehead as though even her touch disgusted him, leaving the albino girl's feet scrabbling uselessly across the floor. Still she reached for him again and again. If the old man was the one who had made her this way, what could she do but beg him?

lines.jp: 「是非もない。儂も、お前を呪い続けるより、今はただ陸に臨みたいのみ───」
lines.en: Very well. I, too, would rather set my eyes upon land now than continue cursing you--

lines.jp: 「その為には、儂の海図が必要でな。海図に陸の位置と針路を書き込んでようやく───嵐も終わりを告げるだろう」
lines.en: But for that, I require my sea chart. Once the position of the land and a course toward it have been drawn upon the chart, the storm will finally come to an end.

lines.jp: 「そして、儂らの長きにわたる漂流も、終わりを迎えるだろう」
lines.en: And our long wandering will end with it.

lines.jp:
「で、まあついでを言うなら、
　そうしてくれたなら、儂、あの大海蛇、どうにかしてやってもよろしいかなぁ、などと愚考いたす次第」
lines.en:
And while we are discussing incidental matters, 
if you do that for me, I might perhaps see fit to deal with the great sea serpent as well.

lines.jp:
茶目っ気の、付け足しのように漏らした言葉だったが、当然一行は、一面針と溶岩で塞がれた荒野の中に、一筋の脱出航路を見いだしたように色めき立つ訳で。
　朔屋は、だが、この老人のぐるぐると変わる雰囲気に胡散臭さを禁じ得ず、なにしろ遙かな世界の悲哀を語るかと思えばクロのような小さな相手に憎悪と怨念を滾らせ、そして今はむずがゆいような茶目っ気の、こういう情緒が安定しない者をまともにするとろくな事がないというのを、皆どうして判らないだろう。普段から自分の事を見ているくせに、とどうにも乗り切れないのであったが。
lines.en:
He offered the words playfully, almost as an afterthought. Naturally, the crew came alive as though they had discovered a single escape route through a wasteland sealed by needles and lava. 
Naomasa, however, could not overlook the suspicious way the old man's air shifted endlessly. One moment he spoke with the sorrow of a distant world, the next he boiled with hatred toward someone as small as Kuro, and now he displayed this coy playfulness. Why did no one understand that treating such an emotionally unstable person seriously could end only in disaster? They watched Naomasa every day, after all. He could not share their enthusiasm.

lines.jp:
「爺、そりゃ本当だろうな。
　今更嘘で俺らを釣ったなら───」
lines.en:
Old man, you'd better be telling the truth. 
If you're trying to lure us with a lie at this stage--

lines.jp:
「どうとってもらっても構わないのだがね。
　ただ、あの生き物を今まで封じておったのは儂だ。なにしろ、お前らが島に来てもすぐには出てこなかっただろ、アレ」
lines.en:
You may take my words however you please. 
But I was the one who kept that creature confined until now. After all, it did not appear the moment you arrived on the island, did it?

lines.jp: 「確かに……」
lines.en: That's true...

lines.jp: 「それで、だ。そのためには」
lines.en: And so, for me to do so...

lines.jp: その為には、海図で針路を示してやることが必要なのだと、老人はクロを突き返しながら。そうすれば元は方舟である島は陸地に辿り着けて、安らかに眠れるのだ、と。
lines.en: To do so, the old man explained while pushing Kuro away, they would have to use the sea chart to mark out a course. Then the island that had once been an ark could reach dry land and finally rest in peace.

lines.jp:
「海図だぁ……？
　気に入りの枕とかでなくってか」
lines.en:
A sea chart...? 
Not a favorite pillow or something?

lines.jp: 「ああ、そうだ。だが、その海図をどこにやってしまったのかが、わからないのだよ」
lines.en: Yes, a sea chart. Unfortunately, I do not know where I put it.

lines.jp:
「ふぅん。海図。
　それでしたら、見覚えがあってよ」
lines.en:
A sea chart, you say. 
In that case, I believe I have seen it.

lines.jp:
「え、あれ、泪さん、
　あなた、いたのかここに」
lines.en:
Huh? Rui? 
You were here?

lines.jp:
朔屋のみならず、他の面子も同様に、失礼ながら仰天の、泪はそれまで一言も口を挟まず下級水夫達の中に混じっていたのだ。
　まるで、ノアの話になど興味もない、と言いたげに。
lines.en:
Not only Naomasa, but everyone else looked equally astonished, rude though that reaction was. Rui had stood among the ordinary sailors without saying a single word. 
It was as though Noah's story held no interest for her whatsoever.

lines.jp:
それで泪が語るらく。
　例の、彼女が散策中に出くわした、塔屋とその中に置かれていた海図の事。
　たいして興味もない事なのか、言葉短かに語ったのが、却って装飾もなく、簡素な織物の筋を辿るように、簡潔に要領を伝えたが、その塔屋の話を聞いて、噴き出したノアもノアであろう。
lines.en:
Rui then told them what she knew: 
during her walk, she had encountered a tower, and inside it a sea chart. 
Perhaps the matter interested her very little, for she spoke only briefly. Yet the lack of ornament made her account concise and clear, like tracing the plain threads of an undecorated cloth. Noah, for his part, burst out laughing when he heard about the tower.

lines.jp:
「鳩の羽根が散らばった、部屋なあ。
　そうかあいつめ、あいつが持って籠もっていたか。じゃあ見つからんわけだ」
lines.en:
A room scattered with dove feathers? 
I see. So she took it and shut herself away there. No wonder I could not find it.

lines.jp:
「なんだよ、誰がどうやって、だよ。
　この島、あんたが造ったんだろ。
　それで見つからないってのは、
　うさん臭くないか」
lines.en:
What do you mean, 'she took it'? 
You built this island, didn't you? 
Isn't it suspicious that there could be something here 
you couldn't find?

lines.jp: 先ほどノアに抱いた印象をどうしても引きずっているし、お大事のクロを虐めてくれた事もあるしで、朔屋はどうしてもこの老人に心を許す気になれず、クロは背後に隠す、自分の心も猜疑心に鎧うで、老人を指摘したのだが。
lines.en: Naomasa could not shake the impression Noah had given him earlier, and the old man had tormented his precious Kuro besides. He could not bring himself to trust him. Keeping Kuro hidden behind his back and armoring his heart in suspicion, he challenged the old man.

lines.jp:
「その骨はな、儂の妻のものだよ。
　晩年、哀しい事に折り合いがあまり良くなくてな。あれはあれで、一人で引き籠もってしまいおった」
lines.en:
Those bones belonged to my wife. 
Sadly, we did not get along well in our later years. She withdrew there alone.

lines.jp: 「儂が近づけないような、そういうセキュリテイでも拵えたんだろう。船のセキュリティの設計担当だったからな、あれは」
lines.en: She must have built some kind of security system to keep me away. She was responsible for designing the ship's security, after all.

lines.jp: 「……ちなみに不仲の原因は」
lines.en: ...And the cause of your estrangement?

lines.jp: そういう余計な事に突っ込む朔屋も朔屋だが、けろりと堪える老人も、どこかがやはり突き抜けていた。
lines.en: Naomasa was himself for prying into something so unnecessary, but the old man who answered without the slightest embarrassment was plainly unusual as well.

lines.jp: 「好みの不一致だ。儂は鴉を好み、妻は鳩を好んだ。夫婦であっても、お互い譲れんことはあるわいな」
lines.en: A difference in taste. I favored ravens, and my wife favored doves. Even between husband and wife, there are certain points on which neither will yield.

lines.jp: と、そこまではまだ、笑い飛ばせ無くもない、微妙な間合いにあったのだが───
lines.en: Up to that point, the mood still hung in a delicate balance where they might almost have laughed it off. But then--

lines.jp:
「ああ、それなら判る。
　ここからのルートは───おや」
lines.en:
Ah, then I understand. 
The route from here is--oh.

lines.jp:
「おやってなんだよおやって。
　なんか良い予感しないよ、
　さっさと言ってくれ」
lines.en:
What do you mean, 'oh'? 
That doesn't sound good. 
Just tell us already.

lines.jp:
「朔屋、なにてめえが仕切ってんだ。
　で、なんなんだよ爺」
lines.en:
Sakuya, who put you in charge? 
Well, old man? What is it?

lines.jp:
そして老人は、泪の説明のように、簡潔に告げた。
　泪が示した、海図の塔屋がある建物には、どうしても大海蛇が陣取る合流点を通っていかなければならない、と。
lines.en:
The old man answered as concisely as Rui had. 
To reach the building with the chart room Rui described, they would inevitably have to pass through the junction occupied by the great sea serpent.

lines.jp: 一同に降りかかった沈黙の意味を計りかねたか、クロが迷路に突っ込まれてそもそもそこでなにをすればいいのかが判らない鼠のように、まだ恐怖の涙に潤む眼差しをしょぼつかせる。朔屋はとりあえず、鍵の掛かった箱があって、でもその錠を開ける鍵は、箱の中に入ってるんだと喩えを借りて説明してやると、納得したのかしないのか、ただ朔屋に身をすり寄せて、うん、と頷く、青年しか今は心を許せる相手がいないかのように。
lines.en: Unable to understand the silence that descended over the group, Kuro blinked eyes still wet with frightened tears, like a mouse dropped into a maze without knowing what it was supposed to do there. Naomasa borrowed an analogy and explained: there was a locked box, but the key to its lock was inside the box. Whether she understood or not, Kuro simply pressed closer to him and nodded, as though he were now the only person she could trust.

lines.jp:
そして、そこに、ノアだった。
　今偶さか想い出したかのように、しかし機を狙ったように、ノアだった。
lines.en:
And then there was Noah. 
He spoke as though the thought had only just occurred to him, yet with the timing of someone who had waited for precisely this moment.

lines.jp:
「なにを鴉といちゃついているんだこの変態。
　お前、暢気に比喩的表現なんぞを用いておるが、あれを放ったのは自分とその鴉だと言う事、判っていないだろう？」
lines.en:
Why are you flirting with a raven, you degenerate? 
You stand there leisurely employing metaphors, but you have not realized that you and that raven were the ones who released the creature, have you?

lines.jp: ───場の沈黙の重さが、朔屋とそしてクロにのみ集中した。
lines.en: --The full weight of the room's silence concentrated upon Naomasa and Kuro alone.

lines.jp: 「……てめえかよ、朔屋」
lines.en: ...It was you, Sakuya?

lines.jp:
「え、ちょっと待って、俺にはなんの事やら、
　心当たりも……」
lines.en:
What? Wait, I don't know what you're talking about. 
I can't think of anything...

lines.jp:
「ほほー……あの汚水溜まったドーム。
　あすこの水門を開けた覚えもないと」
lines.en:
Oh, really? That dome full of filthy water. 
You do not recall opening its floodgate?

lines.jp:
「いや、覚えてるよ。だってあれ豪い硬くて、
　手の皮が剥けそうに───いたいっ」
lines.en:
No, I remember that. The thing was incredibly stiff, 
and it nearly tore the skin off my hands--ow!

lines.jp:
肩を掴んだ万力は、シサムの手。
　睨みつける眸に出会って、朔屋は悲鳴を上げ損ねた。瞋恚でザウエルより燃えていた。乳や臀に性的な悪戯を仕掛けた時の怒声や拳足は、優しく親しい微笑みのようなものなのだと知った、今知って知らなければ良かったと後悔した。
lines.en:
The vise gripping his shoulder was Sisam's hand. 
When Naomasa met her glare, his scream died in his throat. Her rage burned brighter than Zauer. Only now did he realize that the shouts, fists, and kicks she gave him when he played lewd pranks on her chest or backside were affectionate smiles by comparison--and immediately wished he had never learned the difference.

lines.jp: 「使えない、使えないと思っていられるうちは、まだましだった、っていうことか」
lines.en: So being merely useless was still the better option, as long as we could keep thinking that was all you were.

lines.jp: 「早く船に戻って手当てしてあげないと、この子、死んじゃうかもしれないのに……朔屋さんの、せいだ」
lines.en: If we don't get him back to the ship and treat him soon, that boy might die... And it's Sakuya's fault.

lines.jp:
「……この人は、単に巡り合わせが悪いだけ。
　そのお陰で、刺されたり海に放りこまれたりしたけれど」
lines.en:
...He simply has terrible luck. 
Though that luck has gotten him stabbed and thrown into the sea before.

lines.jp: 航海士ばかりではない。日頃は朔屋に厚意的な者達までも、見下げたような眼差しで、
lines.en: It was not only the navigators. Even those normally well disposed toward Naomasa looked down upon him with contempt.

lines.jp: 「きっちりそん時にくたばってりゃよかったんだ」
lines.en: Should've had the decency to die back then.

lines.jp: 「なんだって余計なことをすんだよ、あんたらはさぁ……」
lines.en: Why do you two always have to meddle with things...?

lines.jp: 「違うの。クロは、みんなにほめてもらいたかっただけ」
lines.en: No. Kuro only wanted everyone to praise her.

lines.jp:
言葉を失い立ち尽くす朔屋を庇うように。
　そもそも一連の結果を招く行動の端を解いたのは、朔屋であるのに。クロが、前に出る、のも滅多にない事。たとえば航海士はそんなにひどくは当たらないし、時々は笑ってくれる人だけれど、やはりクロにとっては厳しく恐いお姉さん。
　けれども、とクロは食い下がった。
　いつもは良く判らなくって失敗する。
　今回もそうかも知れない。
　でも今回は、誰かに言いつけられた仕事を失敗したんじゃない。
　今回は───
lines.en:
Kuro stepped forward as though to shield the speechless Naomasa--though it was Naomasa who had set the whole chain of events in motion.
 Kuro almost never put herself forward. The Chief Mates were not always cruel to her and sometimes even smiled, but to Kuro they remained stern, frightening older sisters.
 Even so, she persisted.
 Usually she failed because she did not understand.
 Perhaps she had failed again this time.
 But this time she had not failed at some task another person ordered her to do.
 This time--

lines.jp: 「クロは、馬鹿にされたり、怒られたりするの、やだっただけ」
lines.en: Kuro was just tired of being laughed at and scolded.

lines.jp:
「それが、いけない、かったの？
　クロは、どうすれば、よかったのかなぁ」
lines.en:
Was that... wrong? 
What was Kuro supposed to do?

lines.jp:
「クロは、みんなみたいになりたいって、
　思っちゃ、だめだったのかな」
lines.en:
Was Kuro wrong to wish 
she could be like everyone else?

lines.jp:
クロがいつになく必死だったのは、それが少女のせめてもの、願いとか夢だとか。
　そういった、彼女のお大事の『きらきら』と同じくらい、いやそれ以上に大切にしたいもので、朔屋に教えもらったものだからで、それがあれば、みんなの中で哀しい気持ちにならなくってすむ、惨めな思いで物陰で蹲っていなくってすむ、と。
　それは、大それた願いだったのかどうか、クロにはよく判らない。
　クロは、なにを願った事など、なかったから。あるとすれば、嵐の中の自分でいたいと言う事だけれど、それだって結局はこの願いの別の現れでしかない。
　願わない、夢も抱かないクロが、ずっと心の底に秘めていた思い。
lines.en:
Kuro fought with such uncharacteristic desperation because this was her one modest wish--her dream.
 It was something she wanted to treasure as much as her precious 'sparkles,' perhaps even more, because Naomasa had taught it to her. With it, she would not have to feel sad among the others or crouch miserably in some hidden corner.
 Kuro did not know whether that was too grand a wish.
 She had never wished for anything before. If she had, it was only to remain the self she became within a storm--and even that was merely another form of this same desire.
 This was the thought that Kuro, who made no wishes and held no dreams, had always hidden at the bottom of her heart.

lines.jp:
拳に爪を食いこませている朔屋がいる。彼にもう少し握力があって、剛毅な心を持っていたなら、血を滲ませた掌で、クロを抱いて庇っていたかも知れない。あるいは皆に殴りかかっていったかも知れない。
　しかしこの時、朔屋にはそういった強い心もなかったし、なにしろ事の張本人なので、クロの哀しいくらい真摯な訴えを、そしてそれが現実と衝突して瓦解していく様を、半笑いで見守っているしかなかった訳で。
lines.en:
Naomasa's fingernails dug into his fists. Had his grip been stronger and his heart more resolute, he might have gathered Kuro protectively into bloodied hands. Perhaps he might even have struck at everyone around them.
 But Naomasa possessed no such strong heart. Besides, he was the one responsible. All he could do was watch with an awkward half-smile as Kuro made her painfully earnest appeal, and as it struck reality and broke apart.

lines.jp:
───半笑い？
　
　クロの哀訴を、砕かれる様を、半笑い？
　
　そうとも朔屋はへらへら笑っていた。
　きっと次は誰かが、こう言うぞ。
　自分のやる事に責任持て。
　とかそういう事だ。
lines.en:
--A half-smile? 

Watching Kuro plead, watching her be broken, with a half-smile? 

Indeed, Naomasa stood there grinning foolishly. 
Surely someone would say it next: 
Take responsibility for what you do. 
Something like that.

lines.jp:
「お前は知らなければならなかった。
　願う、祈るだけならいい。
　ただし、行動したならば。
　それがどういう意図であろうとも」
lines.en:
You needed to learn. 
There is nothing wrong with wishing or praying. 
But once you act, 
whatever your intention may have been...

lines.jp: 「その行動の責任を取らなくてはならないことを、クロ、お前は知るべきだった」
lines.en: You must accept responsibility for the consequences. Kuro, you should have learned that.

lines.jp:
ほら、ござった。
　あまりに予想通りで、朔屋はもう大笑いしたくなったが、こらえる術は知っていた。彼自身が何度となく通過した道だったから、身の御し様は知っていた。
　挫折、躓き、青春の蹉跌とかなんだとか。さんざん経験してきて、落ち着いた結論は、ここらへんの足許に転がった石っころで転んで、立ち上がれる人間ばかりでは……ああ、もういいや。
lines.en:
There it was. 
It followed his prediction so perfectly that Naomasa almost wanted to burst out laughing, but he knew how to restrain himself. He had traveled this road many times and knew how to conduct himself upon it. 
Failure, stumbling, the setbacks of youth, or whatever one called it. He had experienced all of them repeatedly and arrived at one calm conclusion: not everyone who trips over a stone lying at their feet can stand back up... Ah, enough.

lines.jp:
俯いて、肩をそばだてボロボロと、ついに声もなく涙ばかりを零し始めたクロの肩を抱き寄せる。もう、皆の目を憚るつもりもなかった。なにしろ、クロにこうしていいのは、こうしてやれるのは、そう自分だけ。信天翁号の中では新前の自分だが、他の皆にはこんな事、させてやらない。
　そもそもできまい。
lines.en:
Kuro bowed her head and raised her shoulders, finally shedding great silent tears. Naomasa pulled her close. He no longer intended to worry about anyone watching. After all, he alone could hold Kuro this way, and he alone could do this for her. He might be the newest member of the Albatross, but he would not let any of the others take this from him. 
Not that they could do it in the first place.

lines.jp: （何故ってあんた達は、やってやれる人間だからな……俺やクロとは違うもんな……）
lines.en: (Because all of you are people who can actually do things... You're different from Kuro and me...)

lines.jp:
凄まじいまでの弱者としての自覚。
　朔屋のある意味強靱な点は、これを抱いていて、酒だ女だと笑っていられる点にあるが、だからといって彼の弱さが克服される訳でも無能が改善される訳でもない。朔屋の無能は巡り合わせが引き寄せるところも大きいけれど、それだけに改善しきれないところもある。
lines.en:
It was an extraordinary awareness of himself as one of the weak.
 One kind of strength Naomasa possessed was that he could carry that knowledge and still laugh about liquor and women. Yet it did not overcome his weakness or cure his incompetence. Much of Naomasa's uselessness was the work of bad luck--and for that very reason, some of it could never be completely corrected.

lines.jp:
朔屋はクロの中に、自分と同じものを見いだしていた。水夫長や航海士、泪には最後まで理解しきる事のできない、弱きものの卑屈なまでのいじましさ、これとこの先どう付き合っていくのか、教示してやれるのはこの船に於いては自分だけだろうと朔屋は、しゃくり上げるクロの肩を抱いて、とりあえずは皆から少し離してやる事にする。
　こういう時には、大勢の体熱や息づかいだけで、自分が死んでしまいたいほど惨めな生き物に思えてくるから。
　隣の部屋に移ろうとする朔屋とクロに、何か言いかけた水夫長へ、
lines.en:
Naomasa saw something of himself in Kuro: the abject, desperate striving of the weak, something the boatswain, the Chief Mates, and Rui could never entirely understand. Naomasa believed he alone aboard this ship could teach her how to live with it from now on. Holding Kuro's shoulders as she sobbed, he decided first to draw her a little away from the others.
 At moments like this, the body heat and breathing of a crowd alone could make you feel like such a miserable creature that you wanted to die.
 As Naomasa and Kuro started toward the next room, the boatswain opened his mouth to say something.

lines.jp: 「……すんませんです。俺ら、ちょっと考え無しでした。あの、後で何やればいいか、聞きますんで」
lines.en: ...Sorry. We acted without thinking. I'll ask what you need us to do later.

lines.jp: 「なんで、今はクロだけでも、ちょっと落ち着かせてくるんで」
lines.en: But right now, I need to help Kuro calm down.

lines.jp:
正直、なにをやらされるかは大体見当が付いている。それを思うと怖ろしくて仕方ない。怖い事はさっさと聞いてしまった方が良いけれど、今はとにかくクロを慰めておかないと。
　朔屋はひたすら卑屈に阿って、続きの部屋にとクロと自分を皆の目から隔離する。
lines.en:
Honestly, Naomasa could already guess what they would be made to do. The thought terrified him. It was usually best to hear frightening news as quickly as possible, but for now he had to comfort Kuro. 
With thoroughly servile deference, Naomasa withdrew into the adjoining room and shut both himself and Kuro away from everyone's eyes.

lines.jp: 苦虫を噛み潰したような水夫長に、キサラが見せたのは皮肉げな、それでいて物事噛み分けたような苦笑だ。
lines.en: Kisara gave the boatswain, whose face looked as though he had bitten into something bitter, a wry but understanding smile.

lines.jp:
「悪役、お疲れ様。水夫長。
　水夫長の長の字は、
　伊達じゃないってわけだ」
lines.en:
Good work playing the villain, Boatswain. 
I suppose the 'chief' in your title 
really does mean something.

lines.jp:
「くだらねえ……名誉挽回の機会？
　知った事かよ」
lines.en:
What a load of garbage... A chance to redeem themselves? 
As if I give a damn.

lines.jp: 唾と共に吐き捨てて、水夫長は禿頭をばりばりと掻いて、床にどっかと腰を落として胡座組み、舞い上がった埃の中でいよいよ厳めしく口元をへしゃげさせる。
lines.en: He spat the words onto the floor, scratched noisily at his bald head, and dropped heavily into a cross-legged seat. Amid the dust his fall kicked up, his mouth twisted into an even fiercer scowl.

lines.jp: と、こちらは、持てる者、できる者の理論だった。
lines.en: Such was the reasoning of those who possessed strength, those who could act.
